claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[cell line], characteristics[cellosaurus accession], characteristics[cellosaurus name], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[sex], characteristics[developmental stage], characteristics[material type] all rows
claims.value: Homo sapiens / HEK-293T cell / CVCL_0063 / HEK293T / kidney / female / fetal stage / cell line
claims.evidence: All knockout and FLAG lines were generated in HEK293T (PRIDE keyword Hek293t; Supp Table 1 lists CRISPR/TALEN knockout clones; Fig. 2c and AP-MS headers use HEK293T as the comparator). Cellosaurus CVCL_0063: Homo sapiens, Female, AG Fetus, derived from HEK293 (embryonic kidney); BTO:0002181 'HEK-293T cell'; developmental stage from Cellosaurus 'Fetus' as HsapDv:0000037 'fetal stage'; organism part kidney UBERON:0002113.

Cellosaurus CVCL_0063 lists no disease for HEK293T (transformed embryonic kidney line); PATO:0000461 normal. The study models complex I deficiency genetically, but no row is a patient sample, so no disease term is broadcast.
summary.txt Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty (light = Arg0/Lys0), Labels1 Arg10;Lys8 for every searched file: one heavy and one light row per raw file.

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C Fixed; Oxidation M, Acetyl Protein N-term, Label:13C(6)15N(4) R (UNIMOD:267), Label:13C(6)15N(2) K (UNIMOD:259) Variable
claims.evidence: parameters.txt 'Fixed modifications Carbamidomethyl (C)'; summary.txt 'Variable modifications Oxidation (M);Acetyl (Protein N-term)', 'Labels1 Arg10;Lys8'. Arg10 = +10.008 Da = UNIMOD:267, Lys8 = +8.014 Da = UNIMOD:259 (batch rule 11: labels MT=Variable). Both searches identical.

The PRIDE record names no digestion enzyme; both MaxQuant searches used 'Trypsin/P', Specific, max 2 missed cleavages (summary.txt), i.e. a tryptic digest; written as Trypsin per batch rule 2. Whole-cell samples were prepared 'as described by Kulak et al.' (PRIDE), a protocol that can use Lys-C with trypsin; no Lys-C is written because no source for this study names it (limitation).

PRIDE data processing: 'Default search parameters for a Arg10 and Lys8 labelled experiment were used' with MaxQuant 1.5.4.1, whose default main-search peptide tolerance is 4.5 ppm (first search 20 ppm). No mqpar.xml was deposited; consistency check on the AP-MS evidence.txt: 88,983 evidences, 99.9th percentile |Mass Error| 0.22 ppm, 51 (0.06%) above 4.5 ppm (max 5.56 ppm). The value rests on the stated use of defaults, not on a deposited parameter file.

MS/MS', 'Activation Type: CID', 'Normalized Coll. Energy: 35.0'; QEP120/P1DAS: 'Q Exactive Plus - Orbitrap MS', 'Scan range 375 to 1800 m/z', 'NCE / stepped NCE 27', Fragmentation_HCD 27; QEP155 (batches H, I): 'Scan range 375 to 1600 m/z'. PRIDE protocol: QE Plus HCD NCE 27 m/z 375-1800; Elite CID 35% m/z 350-1500. Fragment tolerances from parameters.txt: 'MS/MS tol. (FTMS) 20 ppm', 'MS/MS tol. (ITMS) 0.5 Da'. Instrument per file from the file-name tag (ELITE180/QEP120/QEP155/P1DAS), confirmed on one file per batch.

claims.evidence: Every RAW file of the PRIDE file list appears once per SILAC channel; each is listed in the summary.txt of the search it went through (combined.zip: 474 files incl. 6 ACPOE files left out here; combined-AP-MS.zip: 15 files).

claims.evidence: PRIDE protocol: 'Data Dependent Acquisition' (top-12 HCD QE Plus; top-20 CID Elite); raw method names '..._Top12_...', 'CID-Top20'.

claims.location: characteristics[genotype] / factor value[genotype] wild type rows
claims.evidence: AP-MS ratio headers are '<bait>FLAG/HEK293T' (Supp Tables S2-S4, S10, S11), i.e. the partner channel is parental HEK293T; Fig. 2c uses HEK293T as the reference line. In every knockout run the partner channel carries the targeted protein at high level (ratio_check), consistent with an unedited HEK293T partner. The paper Methods (paywalled) were not read; 'wild type' = parental HEK293T is the reading of these sources.

claims.location: comment[sdrf version], comment[sdrf template], comment[sdrf annotation tool]
claims.value: v1.1.0; ms-proteomics v1.2.0, human v1.1.0, cell-lines v1.1.0; sdrf-skills v0.1.0
claims.evidence: Batch rules 1 and 10. Templates: human cell line samples measured by MS.

claims.location: comment[label] per row; channel -> sample map
claims.value: file tag HL: knockout/bait cells = SILAC heavy, HEK293T control = SILAC light; tag LH: the reverse
claims.evidence: Explicit: Supp Data 'Column definitions' — 'X-000-YYY-ZZ ... ZZ, label orientation identifier (either HL or LH)'; AP-MS tables name the HL experiments 'Expt. 1/2 H/L NDUFAB1FLAG/HEK293T...' and the LH experiment 'Expt. 3 L/H NDUFAB1FLAG/HEK293T...' (same pattern in S3, S4, S10, S11), so HL = FLAG cells heavy. PRIDE: raw names include 'applicable label orientation'. Data check: AP-MS H/L of the bait protein log2 +3.1 to +6.1 in all 10 HL runs and -3.6 to -5.0 in all 5 LH runs; knockout runs: H/L of the knocked-out protein is negative in every HL experiment with a value (e.g. NDUFA9 Q-025 -3.48, NDUFB6 H-096 -3.78, NDUFB11 M-149 -5.89) and positive in every LH experiment with a value (e.g. NDUFA8 M-144 +3.69, NDUFB9 V-225 +3.74); 89 of the 117 annotated mitochondrial experiments quantify the target and all 89 agree in sign; none contradicts. Whole-cell experiments are encoded the same way and match Supp Table S5 column names (e.g. FS6-1_1/2/3 HL,HL,LH = W.1-3.NDUFS6 HL,HL,LH).

claims.location: characteristics[genotype] / factor value[genotype] knockout rows; source name
claims.value: <gene> knockout (38 lines: 30 accessory subunits NDUFA1-A3,A5-A13,AB1,B1-B11,C1,C2,S4-S6,V3; assembly factors NDUFAF1, NDUFAF2, NDUFAF4, NDUFAF6, TIMMDC1, DMAC1, ATP5SL; COA6)
claims.evidence: Gene from the raw file name (PRIDE: names carry the 'knockout cell line being studied'); Supp Table 1 lists the CRISPR/TALEN knockout clones for each gene (NDUFA9 and COA6 KOs generated previously); Supp Table S5 reports 'Mean Log2 ratio <gene>' for exactly these lines (ACPOE excluded, see limitations); target protein depleted in each quantified experiment (ratio_check). NDUFAB1 KO line: Supp Table 1 clones ACP1-1/ACP1-3 'KO (NDUFAB1)' and Ext Data Fig. 3 (KO complemented to survive); yeast ACP1 (P32463) is detected in the knockout channel of O-168..170 (H/L 5.37 in HL, 0.35/0.38 in LH), so this line expresses yeast ACP1; the genotype is written as 'NDUFAB1 knockout' without asserting the rescue construct.

PRIDE: 'SILAC labelled, 8M UREA solubilised mitochondria analysed through a single injection' and 'SDC solubilised whole-cell starting material fractionated over SCX'. Mitochondrial runs = single-injection numbered files (T1..T5 repeats); whole-cell = P1DAS_2016* files with F1-F6 (experimentalDesignTemplate Fraction 1-6; raw path '20160506_WC_SILAC_BATCHA'). GO:0005739 mitochondrion; 'whole cell' is free text in this custom column (batch rule 16).

claims.location: comment[technical replicate], comment[fraction identifier], comment[fractionation method] rows
claims.value: mito: T<n> -> technical replicate n, fraction 1, fractionation not applicable; whole-cell: F1-F6 -> fraction 1-6, technical replicate 1, SCX (PRIDE:0000561)
claims.evidence: experimentalDesignTemplate groups T1/T2/T3 of one run in one Experiment (e.g. 001+ELITE180_D-040-NDUFA1-HL_T1..T3 -> D-040-NDUFA1-HL); the T1/T2 raw headers of 001ELITE180_D-040 show the same vial (RB5) re-injected; the MaxQuant 'Fraction' values 8/10/12 for these files are matching groups ('Experimental groups ... were given odd numbered fractions to avoid falsely matched identifications', PRIDE), not fractions. 035ELITE180_R-005 has only T1 and T3 deposited, kept as technical replicates 1 and 3. Whole-cell F1-F6 = SCX fractions per Kulak et al. (PRIDE).

claims.value: 1..n per genotype group; wild type numbered 1..150 across all 150 experiments (117 mitochondrial + 33 whole-cell)
claims.evidence: Each knockout line was measured in three independent SILAC experiments ('n = 3 biological replicates', Fig. 2d, Ext Data Fig. 8-9; triplicate columns in Supp Table S5). Within a genotype group the mitochondrial and whole-cell experiments (and the two NDUFA13 batches R and I) are numbered consecutively, never reusing a number (batch rule 3). Each experiment's HEK293T partner is given its own number in the wild-type group because the deposit does not say whether control cultures were shared; this may over-count control cultures (limitation).

limitations: Paper Methods are behind the Nature paywall and were not read (not bypassed); sample preparation details (culture medium, reduction/alkylation reagents, passage) are therefore not available. PRIDE lists 'iodoacetamide derivatized residue' and cites Kulak et al. 2014 (an iST protocol that uses chloroacetamide); reagents left out rather than guessed.
Precursor tolerance 4.5 ppm rests on the PRIDE statement that MaxQuant defaults were used (no mqpar.xml deposited).
Instrument settings (scan range, NCE, analyzer) were read from one raw file per acquisition batch (25 files), not from every file.
Wild-type HEK293T partner channels: each experiment's control is given a distinct biological replicate number; whether control SILAC cultures were shared between experiments is not documented.

PRIDE lists two publications. PMID 27626371 (Stroud et al., Nature 2016) generated the data. PMID 32161263 (Zhang et al., Nat Commun 2020, BRAWNIN) reanalysed the mitochondrial raw files with SearchGUI/PeptideShaker and is not the source of any sample metadata.
Digestion enzyme: no source for this study names it; Trypsin is taken from the search rule (Trypsin/P). The whole-cell protocol cites Kulak et al., which may have used Lys-C in addition.

Partial scope: the 6 raw files of experiments O-171..173 'ACPOE' (091QEP120_O-171-ACPOE-LH_T1/T2, 092QEP120_O-172-ACPOE-LH_T1/T2, 093QEP120_O-173-ACPOE-LH_T1/T2) are left out: the identity of the ACPOE line is not defined in the paper, Supplementary Information or Supplementary Data (only 'Mean Log2 ratio ACPOE' in Table S5). Data suggest yeast ACP1 over-expression in cells with normal NDUFAB1 (NDUFAB1 H/L ~1.15, yeast ACP1 P32463 H/L 0.07 in an LH run), but that is inference. See annotations/BLOCKED.md.
experimentalDesignTemplate.txt of combined.zip lists 6 runs (124ELITE180_K-117/118/119-NDUFV1, T1/T2) that were neither deposited nor searched (absent from summary.txt); no rows exist for them.
The NDUFAB1 knockout line expresses yeast ACP1 (detected in its channel); the rescue construct is not encoded in the genotype value.
Whole-cell clone tokens in file names (e.g. FA8-22 = NDUFA8-22, FB4-7 = NDUFB4-7 per Supp Table 1) are not encoded; FS5-A9 matches no clone in Supp Table 1.
